caption: Graph output: a sub-graph's colour pin - previewed on its own, the colour it gives is what the LEDs show
why: A piece of graph you use again and again - a fire, a sparkle layer, a scroll - can become a node of its own: a sub-graph. Graph input and Graph output are its pins: each Graph input becomes an input of the node, each Graph output an output.

Select nodes and Node > Fold into a sub-graph makes one, with these pins already in place. Its neighbours: Send and Receive carry values within one graph; Graph input and output carry them in and out of a sub-graph.
steps: The scrolling **Palette** colour goes into the Graph output's **value**.
**name** is colour: the output pin of the node this graph becomes. **type** is color, so the pin carries a colour.
With no Output in the graph, the first colour Graph output is what the LEDs show while the graph is previewed on its own.
A **Graph input** named speed sets how fast it scrolls.

try.label: Rename the pin
try.text: name paint: the node made from this graph will have an output called paint.
